newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says studies cancelling Talara refinery sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru says studies cancelling Talara refinery sale.

text.p: Concerned about a lack of influence over local gasoline prices, the Peruvian government said Tuesday it was considering cancelling an important part of its oil privatization program by not selling the Talara refinery.
"We are studying a series of possibilities ... (one) possibility is to not privatize Talara," the government's privatization chief, Jorge Gonzalez Izquierdo, said.
The government was set to sell the country's second largest refinery in February.

"In case, along the way in the privatization process, you see there is a danger that the market is generating mechanisms to create non-competitive prices ... the government has taken the precaution of making a halt in the process and studying the problem," Izquierdo said.

The privatization chief added the government was also studying the possibility of keeping in government hands state- run Petroperu's terminals "to allow fuel - diesel or gasoline - to be imported and so allow market regulation."
The Talara refinery auction was part of Petroperu's piecemeal privatization.

Within Peru, the series of oil sales has been the most controversial aspect of the government's sweeping privatization program that has also seen sell-offs in the mining, fishing, telecommunications and electricty sectors.
Criticism of the oil privatizations, however, appeared to have died down in June following the $180.5 million sale of a 60 percent stake in the country's largest refinery, La Pampilla sale.
But recent gasoline price hikes have again focused opposition to the sales.
As well as the La Pampilla stake, the government has also auctioned its lubricants unit, Petrolube, and the rights to explore and exploit several oil blocks.
